A question is a sentence that goes up

English builds questions with a helper and a word-order change: \"You speak English\" becomes \"Do you speak English?\". Italian does none of that: you keep the sentence exactly as it is and raise your voice at the end. No inversion, no \"do\".

StatementQuestion
Parli inglese.Parli inglese?
Sei francese.Sei francese?
Marco lavora il sabato.Marco lavora il sabato?
Non abiti qui.Non abiti qui?

The rule: a yes/no question keeps the word order of the statement; only the intonation changes.

The trap: looking for an equivalent of \"do\" or \"are you\". There isn't one. Sei francese? is enough, in writing and in speech.

To answer: sì or no, then the sentence, with non before the verb for the negative.

Parli spagnolo? — No, non parlo spagnolo.Do you speak Spanish? — No, I don't speak Spanish.

Watch the accent: è (it is) is not e (and).

L'autobus è in orario?Is the bus on time?
", "

Question words

ItalianEnglishExample
chiwhoChi è? — È Anna.
che cosa (or cosa)whatChe cosa studi?
dovewhereDove abiti?
di dovewhere from (origin)Di dove sei? — Sono di Lione.
quandowhenQuando lavori?
comehowCome ti chiami? — Mi chiamo Luca.
perchéwhy, becausePerché studi l'italiano? — Perché amo l'Italia.

The rule: the question word goes first and the verb follows immediately; if the subject is a noun, it comes after the verb.

Dove lavora Marco?Where does Marco work? (not \"Dove Marco lavora?\" — and no word for \"does\")

A single word, perché, is used both to ask (why) and to answer (because). It takes an acute accent: é.

Two little contractions with è: dove + è = dov'è, come + è = com'è. But qual è is written without an apostrophe.

", "

How much and which: they agree

Unlike English \"how many\" and \"which\", quanto and quale agree with the noun that follows.

SingularPlural
Masculinequanto tempo?quanti anni? quanti fratelli?
Femininequanta acqua?quante lingue? quante sorelle?

One word covers both \"how much\" and \"how many\": it's the ending that changes. How many languages? = Quante lingue? On its own before a verb, quanto stays masculine: Quanto costa? (How much does it cost?)

Quale has one form for masculine and feminine singular, and one for the plural: quali. English often says \"what\" where Italian uses quale.

Quali lingue parli?Which languages do you speak?
Qual è l'indirizzo di Luca?What is Luca's address?

Four ready-made questions

QuestionAnswer
Come ti chiami?Mi chiamo…
Di dove sei?Sono di…
Che lavoro fai?Sono architetto. / Lavoro in banca.
Quanti anni hai?Ho trent'anni.

In Che lavoro fai?, fai means \"you do\": learn the question as a whole; the verb fare will come later.

title: Asking questions
why: After essere, avere and -are verbs, the learner can answer; now they need to ask questions themselves, without copying the English "do" and inversion. A single point, practiced slowly, with verbs already covered.
